extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news organizations, news startups, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational 'About' page for the Nieman Journalism Lab describing its mission, goals, audience participation, staff, reuse licensing, and procedural details (e.g., fellowship deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Journalism Lab is an attempt to help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explains the context: the Internet has produced abundant information while destabilizing old business models; the Lab aims to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail, find good ideas for others to steal, help reporters and editors adjust to online work, help traditional news organizations find ways to survive, and help new startups that will complement or supplant them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage selection criterion: highlight innovation and analyze success/failure
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit editorial standard: prioritize coverage of innovative experiments in journalism and analyze the factors that contributed to their outcomes (successes and failures) so others can learn from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionability/reproducibility: find ideas others can copy
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to find good ideas for others to steal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial preference for reporting that surfaces practical, transferable ideas or tactics that other journalists or organizations can adopt or adapt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for practitioner adaptation: help reporters and editors adjust to online labors
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should be useful in helping individual journalists change practices, adopt new tools, or learn skills needed in digital reporting and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational focus: help traditional news organizations survive and aid startups
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to help traditional news organizations find a way to survive; we want to help the new crop of startups that will complement — or supplant — them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and research attention should include business-model experiments, sustainability strategies, and analysis of startups that impact the news ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone guideline: maintain fundamental optimism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab frames its mission positively: acknowledge challenges but emphasize constructive, solution-oriented perspectives rather than purely pessimistic accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community participation: emphasize reader contributions and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among them are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas. Tell us what’s happening around you, or what should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab encourages readers to submit tips, examples, and ideas; community input is treated as a substantive part of the site's research and coverage strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default copyright attribution requirement: when reusing content, attribute to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the original author, preferably with a link back to the original content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content reuse license: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions spelled out on the page: (a) do not use for commercial purposes, (b) attribute to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the work’s author (preferably with a link), and (c) release any derivative work under a similar license. Examples provided: translating the site, redistributing posts to students, using the Twitter feed as song lyrics. For any other uses, contact the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowship application deadlines (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual deadline to apply for a fellowship is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural, calendar-based requirement relevant to prospective Nieman Fellows; applicants should observe these deadlines annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channels and engagement: multiple distribution and conversation pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab provides multiple ways to follow and engage: daily or weekly email, Fuego (real-time links), Encyclo (encyclopedia), iPhone app, Facebook, Twitter, RSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site signals preferred and available channels for consumption and participation; contributors and readers are encouraged to use these channels to stay current and contribute.
